bug.title: The hardened child admits a disallowed import issued from inside a callback the signal passes to a trusted library, because the guard trusts any trusted frame anywhere up the stack
bug.symptoms: orchestrator._sandbox_child._admit admits a non-allowlisted import when _trusted_root_in_stack finds a frame belonging to polars, numpy, pyarrow or contract anywhere above the importing frame. A signal that passes a Python callback to a trusted library runs that callback with the library's own frames on the stack, so a disallowed import performed inside the callback is admitted. A top-level disallowed import is still correctly refused, and a benign signal still runs; only the via-callback path escapes. In the unisolated hardened-subprocess executor (feature 2) the import guard is the only barrier, so this lets agent-authored code reach the host filesystem and process APIs. Under gVisor (feature 5) the same attempt is contained by the sandbox, so this is defense-in-depth there and a true escape only when unisolated.
bug.reproduction_steps: Run the child bootstrap over a signal whose body invokes a trusted library's row-wise callback mechanism, and whose callback performs an import outside AGENT_IMPORTS_ALLOWLIST. The import is admitted and the callback's side effect reaches the host, where a top-level import of the same name raises disallowed_import.
bug.expected: - The signal source frame (SIGNAL_SOURCE_FILENAME) poisons an import: when any frame in the importing call stack belongs to the signal source, only a name on AGENT_IMPORTS_ALLOWLIST is admitted, no matter what trusted frames sit above or below it. A disallowed import reachable from agent code — directly or through a library callback — is refused with the existing disallowed_import ImportError and classified crash. - A trusted library's own lazy import during execution, with no signal-source frame in its stack, is still admitted, so legitimate polars/numpy/pyarrow lazy imports keep working. The existing module-load-time trusted-dependency chain is unchanged. - The allowlisted names still import from anywhere, including from a callback. - Tests, driven through the real child subprocess, cover: a disallowed import inside a library callback (refused, no host side effect); a disallowed import nested one callback deeper (refused); an allowlisted import inside a callback (admitted); and a benign signal that uses a library callback without importing (clean scores). A test asserts no sentinel file the signal attempts to create ever appears.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator/_sandbox_child.py _admit returns True whenever _trusted_root_in_stack(sys._getframe(2)) finds a trusted root in the chain. The walk was meant to let a trusted package's own deep dependency loading through, but it also trusts agent code executing within a trusted library's callback, because that agent frame sits below the library's frames in the same stack.
bug.constraints: The bootstrap still imports only the standard library, polars, pyarrow and the contract member No network access and no real credential in any test No file outside the two listed is edited The result channel, the request framing and the fail-class vocabulary are unchanged Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
